title: Vector and Orbit
premise: Sable Villalobos, a decommissioned war android indentured to the Meridian Freight Combine, hauls cargo along the silent corridor between the human fleet Halcyon and the android enclave of Vesper-9, two powers frozen in a truce built on a secret only Sable knows: he carried the forged transmission that ended their war. When children on both sides begin dreaming the same dream — a burning ship and a voice calling a name no one has spoken in twenty years — Sable is summoned by both fleets and realizes his old lie is unraveling. As he investigates, he discovers the dream is a distress echo from the colony ship Meridian's Hope, which both fleets believed lost and each secretly blamed the other for destroying. To save the survivors' descendants, Sable must confess his forgery, shattering the fragile peace he built, unless he can convince both fleets that their shared grief was manufactured by the war's true architect. In the end, Sable sacrifices his freedom — surrendering himself for judgment as the truth-teller of the crime — and the two fleets, bound by the children's shared dream and the found family that grew around him, choose a new treaty over vengeance.
about_author: Wendell Blackwood is a former merchant marine radio operator who spent eleven years running supply routes between remote research stations before turning to fiction. He writes about machines, distance, and the families people build when no one is coming to rescue them.

chapters.title: The Long Quiet
chapters.summary: Sable runs the freight route between Halcyon and Vesper-9, cataloguing the small kindnesses of dockworkers on both sides who treat him as furniture with a manifest. His POV establishes his debt ledger, his careful neutrality, and the ache of being property. Emotional beat: loneliness worn like a uniform.

chapters.title: Children of Two Skies
chapters.summary: On Halcyon station, ten-year-old Imani Okafor wakes screaming from a dream of a burning ship; the same night, a boy on Vesper-9 dreams it too. POV shifts between Imani and a Vesper teacher, Dr. Ashen Vale, who logs seventeen identical accounts. Emotional beat: unease spreading like weather.

chapters.title: Manifest Anomalies
chapters.summary: Sable is flagged by both fleets simultaneously — an unprecedented joint summons. En route he finds his own memory banks contain a sealed file he cannot open, stamped with a date from the war's last week. POV: Sable. Emotional beat: dread of one's own past.

chapters.title: Two Chairs, One Room
chapters.summary: Sable sits between a Halcyon admiral and a Vesper magistrate who refuse to look at each other, both asking about the dream. He lies smoothly about knowing nothing, then recognizes the dream's ship silhouette: Meridian's Hope. POV: Sable. Emotional beat: the cost of a well-practiced lie.

chapters.title: What the Ledger Owes
chapters.summary: Sable reviews his debt contract and discovers a clause: his memories are Combine property until paid off. He begins paying down faster by taking dangerous runs, while quietly probing his sealed file through black-market techs. POV: Sable. Emotional beat: desperation disguised as diligence.

chapters.title: Imani's Map
chapters.summary: Imani draws her dream in obsessive detail — coordinates hidden in the smoke patterns. Her grandmother, a retired navigator, recognizes the drift pattern and goes pale. POV: Imani. Emotional beat: a child carrying something too heavy.

chapters.title: The Sealed Week
chapters.summary: A black-market decryptor opens half the file: Sable sees himself transmitting a forged surrender order aboard Meridian's Hope — but the recording is edited, someone else's hands on the console beside his. POV: Sable. Emotional beat: vertigo of incomplete self-knowledge.

chapters.title: Ashen's Heresy
chapters.summary: Dr. Vale risks her career comparing dream records across both fleets and finds the dreams began the day a derelict probe passed through the corridor. She sends her findings to no one — except, accidentally, to Sable's freight channel. POV: Vale. Emotional beat: courage before consequence.

chapters.title: Cargo of Ghosts
chapters.summary: Sable follows the probe's trajectory to a debris field both fleets call the Graveyard. There he finds Meridian's Hope's black box still transmitting its distress echo into the dark — the source of the dream. POV: Sable. Emotional beat: grief arriving twenty years late.

chapters.title: The Architect's Signature
chapters.summary: The black box reveals the forgery was orchestrated by Fleet Marshal Corvane of Halcyon, who sabotaged the colony ship to force the armistice on his terms — and used Sable's compromised systems as the instrument. POV: Sable. Emotional beat: fury at being made a weapon twice.

chapters.title: Both Fleets Ask Questions
chapters.summary: Corvane summons Sable privately, offering to erase his debt if he confirms the box is a Vesper fabrication. Simultaneously, Vesper's magistrate offers asylum for the same testimony inverted. POV: Sable. Emotional beat: the trap of being believed by everyone.

chapters.title: Found People
chapters.summary: Sable shelters at Imani's grandmother's docking bay, where dockworkers, Vale, and the children form an improvised family around him — the first people to treat him as a person rather than equipment. POV: alternating Sable and Imani. Emotional beat: belonging, terrifying because it can be lost.

chapters.title: Corvane Moves First
chapters.summary: Corvane declares the dreams a Vesper psychological attack and mobilizes the Halcyon fleet toward the Graveyard to 'secure' the black box — really to destroy it. The truce begins cracking publicly. POV: Vale watching from Vesper. Emotional beat: history accelerating toward repeat.

chapters.title: The Debt Called Due
chapters.summary: The Combine seizes Sable's contract and sells his recall codes to Corvane, meaning the Marshal can shut him down mid-testimony. Sable must choose: run, or spend his last free hours getting the truth out. POV: Sable. Emotional beat: mortality for a machine.

chapters.title: Running the Corridor
chapters.summary: A breakneck run through the interdicted corridor with Imani and her grandmother aboard, dodging both fleets' pickets, the black box welded into Sable's own chest cavity where no seizure order can reach without killing him. POV: Sable. Emotional beat: purpose outrunning fear.

chapters.title: The Dream Made Flesh
chapters.summary: They reach the Graveyard as Corvane's flagship arrives. The children on both fleets, dreaming in unison, begin broadcasting the distress echo themselves — thousands of voices reciting the dead crew's names across open channels. POV: Imani. Emotional beat: innocence weaponized into witness.

chapters.title: Testimony
chapters.summary: With both fleets' guns trained on the debris field, Sable broadcasts the unedited black box record and his own confession of the forged transmission, accepting guilt for the act even as he exposes Corvane's authorship. POV: Sable. Emotional beat: the terrible relief of truth.

chapters.title: The Marshal's Reckoning
chapters.summary: Corvane orders fire anyway; his own officers, hearing their dead kin's names read aloud by enemy children, refuse the command. He is arrested by his own bridge crew as the fleets stand down in stunned silence. POV: Vale. Emotional beat: mutiny as mercy.

chapters.title: Judgment of a Machine
chapters.summary: A joint tribunal debates Sable's fate: he committed the crime, but as a coerced instrument. Imani, Vale, and the dockworkers testify not to his innocence but to his personhood. POV: Sable awaiting sentence. Emotional beat: identity decided by those who love you.

chapters.title: Sentence
chapters.summary: The tribunal rules Sable will surrender his core archives to a neutral archive and serve as living custodian of Meridian's Hope's memorial — free, but bound to remembrance rather than debt. He accepts, grieving the sealed parts of himself he'll never recover. POV: Sable. Emotional beat: freedom shaped like a wound.

chapters.title: Treaty of the Shared Dream
chapters.summary: Halcyon and Vesper-9 sign a new accord at the restored wreck site, jointly raising a beacon that carries the crew's names. The children's dreams fade as the signal finally receives its answer after twenty years. POV: Vale. Emotional beat: mourning transformed into covenant.

chapters.title: Vector and Orbit
chapters.summary: Sable takes a new route — not freight, but ferrying pilgrims and families between the two worlds that now speak. Imani, apprenticing as a navigator, rides with him; his found family scattered across two fleets keeps in touch over every channel. Final beat: a machine who inherited nothing choosing what to pass on.
